headline: Sterling is about 1.3115 dollars on Friday morning, close to its low for 2026, as a firm Fed and a fall in US shares keep the dollar near its highest in 19 months. UK retail sales for October rose 0.7% against no change expected, but gave the pound only a small lift.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting, published on 18 November, show that nearly all officials expect rates will need to rise further, and Governor Waller has called for the Fed to be more aggressive, including a possible half point rise. CME FedWatch put the chance of a December rise at 97.3% for a quarter point and 2.7% for half a point on 20 November, FXStreet reported.

drivers.title: The gap between US and UK rates
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, and FXStreet reported on 19 November that a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December would take US rates above UK rates. UK inflation of 3.6% in October, with softer services prices, led traders to trim bets on a December Bank of England rise, and the UK ten year gilt yield fell 8.2 basis points to 5.29% on Wednesday, FXStreet reported on 20 November.

drivers.title: Shares and the dollar
drivers.text: US shares fell about 2% on Thursday, FXStreet reported, and the pound has fallen about 400 pips in eleven sessions from a high near 1.3500 on 4 November. Weaker shares tend to support the dollar as a safe haven, and Spectra Markets, quoted by FXStreet, also pointed to dollar buying by companies ahead of Thanksgiving and by funds rebalancing.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Iran's navy said two oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, and Houthi missiles were fired at Riyadh, FXStreet reported on 20 November. US crude held steady as the tanker reports offset rising US stocks of crude, and Gulf tension tends to support the dollar.

lower: Further falls in shares or fresh tension in the Gulf, which tend to lift the dollar as a safe haven and mean fewer dirhams per pound.
Firm talk from Fed Governor Waller on Friday afternoon of a larger December rise, which would support the dollar.
higher: Firm comments from Bank of England officials such as Megan Greene, who said on Thursday that the bigger risk is doing too little on inflation, which would tend to lift the pound, as would further strong UK figures like October's retail sales.
A recovery in shares or softer US figures, which would ease the dollar and mean more dirhams per pound.
watch: With the Michigan figures out, no further major US or UK figure is due this week, and next week's calendar will appear here as it is published. US markets close on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving, which tends to thin trading in the dollar; softer US news would tend to help someone selling pounds for dirhams, and firmer US news would mean fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar firms late on Friday
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3115 at 19:51 Dubai to about 1.3099 by 20:03 and stayed near 1.3098 to 1.3103 through 20:36, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0989 to about 1.0975, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move, which came in the minutes before 4pm London time, when many currency deals are priced, and with no US or UK figure due.

feed.title: US consumer mood and price fears have barely moved the pound
feed.text: The final University of Michigan reading of US consumer sentiment for November came in at 51.5, in line with the 51.5 InvestingLive's poll expected and a touch below the 51.7 on the calendar, while Americans' expectations for inflation over the next year fell to 3.7% from 4.3% in the first estimate. Lower expected inflation would usually ease pressure for Fed rises and soften the dollar slightly, but with a December rise already almost fully priced the figures made little difference. GBP/USD was about 1.3110 at 19:00 Dubai, dipped to 1.3105 by 19:05, rose to about 1.3117 by 19:15 and was back near 1.3113 by 19:38.

feed.title: Sterling has risen as the dollar eases across the board
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3099 at 16:53 Dubai to about 1.3126 by 17:08 and held near 1.3120 to 1.3125 through 17:38, while EUR/USD rose from about 1.0975 to about 1.0989 over the same minutes, so the dollar eased generally rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move; it came as US Treasury yields fell across the curve, with the 10 year yield at 4.98% and the rout in shares deepening, FXStreet reported. Fed Governor Waller was due to speak at 17:25 Dubai, and GBP/USD moved little around that time, staying near 1.3120.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped and recovered as US yields fall
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3110 at 15:43 Dubai to about 1.3093 by 16:00, while EUR/USD fell by only about a third as much, so the pound was a little weaker in its own right; no report read names a single item of news behind the dip, and FXStreet at 15:55 Dubai again put the pound's weakness down to markets pricing a December Fed rise at 97.3%. From about 16:35 Dubai the dollar eased across the board as the fall in shares deepened and the 10 year US Treasury yield slipped below 5% to 4.98%, FXStreet reported, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3095 at 16:34 to about 1.3109 by 16:38, with EUR/USD rising alongside it.

feed.title: Sterling has eased as investors turn to the dollar
feed.text: Investors kept moving into the dollar as a safe haven during the European morning, as the fall in shares over stretched technology valuations widened, and with markets fully pricing a quarter point Fed rise in December, OCBC said in a note reported by FXStreet. No single piece of news set off the move. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3119 just before 08:00 London time to about 1.3096 by 08:46 and stayed near there before edging back to 1.3103 by 09:35.

feed.title: UK shoppers spent more than expected in October
feed.text: UK retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October against no change expected, helped by households stocking up on long-life food after the government's Be Ready campaign and by colder weather lifting clothing sales; sales were 2.3% higher than a year earlier against 1.7% expected. Stronger spending tends to support the case for further Bank of England rises and so lifts the pound, but the reaction was small: GBP/USD rose from 1.3111 to 1.3117 within a minute, then settled near 1.3113 before edging up to about 1.3117 a quarter of an hour later.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar eases slightly
feed.text: GBP/USD edged up from about 1.3097 at 07:40 Dubai to about 1.3105 by 09:00, dipped to about 1.3097 at 09:40 and then rose to about 1.3112 by 10:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0969 to 1.0983, so the dollar eased a little across the board rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind it; Reuters reported early on Friday that the dollar index was steady near its highest since April 2025 and that the 10 year US Treasury yield was near a one week low, even as Asian shares fell sharply. UK retail sales for October follow at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped to a new low for the year as shares fall overnight
feed.text: US shares fell about 2% on Thursday, FXStreet reported, and the dollar stayed firm near its 19 month high, helped by a firm Fed and, in the view of Spectra Markets quoted by FXStreet, by overseas buyers of the Anthropic share sale buying an estimated $10 billion to $15 billion (about £7.6 billion to £11.5 billion). A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3092 at 01:15 Dubai to about 1.3077 by 01:30, touched about 1.3074 at 06:10 and had recovered to about 1.3096 by 07:35; EUR/USD fell by a similar share overnight, so the move came from the dollar rather than from UK news.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped and recovered as the dollar firms briefly
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3112 at 21:00 Dubai to about 1.3090 by 21:07, recovered to about 1.3113 by 21:20 and stood near 1.3106 at 21:35. EUR/USD dipped over the same minutes, from about 1.0978 to 1.0969, so the dollar firmed briefly across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the dip; FXStreet still describes the dollar as supported by the Fed's firm stance after minutes showing almost all officials expect further rises.

feed.title: Sterling has fallen to a fresh low as the rate gap with the US widens
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3141 at 19:00 Dubai to about 1.3107 by 19:22, below its October low, then steadied near 1.3114 at 19:36; EUR/USD fell over the same minutes, from about 1.0990 to 1.0975, so the dollar firmed broadly and the pound slipped a little further, which means fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news at 19:00 Dubai. FXStreet said at 19:22 Dubai that softer US jobless claims and factory figures had not dented bets on a December Fed rise, priced near 95%, while softer UK inflation has cut the chance of a December Bank of England rise to about 80%, so the gap in expected interest rates is weighing on the pound.

feed.title: The dollar has eased after softer US factory and jobs figures
feed.text: The Philadelphia Fed factory survey fell to 6.3 in November against 20.6 expected, its lowest since May, and new claims for jobless benefits rose to 203,000 against 198,000 expected, although the survey's price measures rose further. Softer activity and a slightly weaker job market make further Fed rises a little less certain, which tends to weaken the dollar and means slightly more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3144 just before the 17:30 Dubai release to about 1.3152 within six minutes, then settled near 1.3149, a modest reaction.

feed.title: Sterling has risen as a brighter market mood eases the dollar
feed.text: European shares rose and US stock futures pointed to a strong open on Thursday, and FXStreet reported at 15:14 Dubai that the better mood had halted the dollar's rally, although expectations of further Fed rises limited its losses. A softer dollar means slightly more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3141 at 13:40 Dubai to about 1.3166 by 14:45 and stood near 1.3162 at 15:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0983 to 1.1005, so the move came from the dollar rather than from UK news.

feed.title: Sterling has firmed as the dollar eases at the London open
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3136 at 11:00 Dubai, as London opened, to about 1.3151 by 11:30 and stood near 1.3151 at 12:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0967 to 1.0981, so the move came from the dollar easing back from its 19 month high rather than from UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind it; FXStreet still describes the dollar as supported by the Fed's firm stance, with CME FedWatch showing about a 93% chance of a December rise.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar steadies
feed.text: GBP/USD recovered from a low near 1.3118 at about 07:10 Dubai to about 1.3136 at 10:38, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0954 to 1.0965, so the move came from the dollar easing slightly from the 19 month high it reached early this morning, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind it; FXStreet still describes the dollar as supported by the Fed's firm stance, with markets pricing a December Fed rise at close to 90%.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped overnight as the dollar firms on Fed rate bets
feed.text: The dollar gained against most major currencies in Asian trade, with the dollar index up 0.12% at about 104.00 by 07:14 Dubai, according to FXStreet, as Wednesday's Fed minutes and Governor Waller's call for a half point rise kept further US rate rises in view. A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD eased from about 1.3149 at 05:00 Dubai to a low near 1.3117 at about 07:15 and stood near 1.3124 at 07:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0974 to 1.0955, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound.

feed.title: Fed minutes back further rate rises
feed.text: The minutes of the Fed's October meeting, out at 23:00 Dubai, show that almost all officials judged further rises would likely be appropriate, some argued for a rise in October itself and a couple suggested a larger rise could be needed in December. That confirms the firm stance markets already expected, which supports the dollar and means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3150 just before the release to about 1.3138 within eight minutes and stood near 1.3137 at 23:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back ahead of the Fed minutes
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from a low near 1.3134 at about 20:40 Dubai to about 1.3152 at 21:29 and stood near 1.3150 at 21:38, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0957 to 1.0972, so the recovery came mainly from a softer dollar and means slightly more dirhams per pound. CNBC reported the US ten year Treasury yield down more than three basis points at about 5.06%, against 5.12% in early Asian trade, and lower US yields tend to weaken the dollar. No report read names a single item of news behind the move, which came in quiet trade ahead of the Fed minutes at 23:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped to around its low for the year
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3155 at 19:40 Dubai to a low near 1.3134 at about 20:20, close to the year's low of about 1.3137, and stood near 1.3138 at 20:38, while EUR/USD fell by a smaller share, from about 1.0964 to 1.0958, so this leg was mainly the pound and means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. FXStreet reported at 19:40 Dubai that Governor Bailey said UK inflation will rise further but that policy is not on a pre-set path, and that traders had cut the chance of a December Bank of England rise to about 80% from about 90% after this morning's slightly softer inflation figure. No report read ties the slide after 19:55 to a single item of news; it came ahead of the Fed minutes at 23:00 Dubai, where Governor Waller's call for a half point Fed rise has left markets expecting US rates to match or pass UK rates.

feed.title: Sterling has barely moved during Governor Bailey's evening speech
feed.text: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey was due to speak at 19:00 Dubai, but by 19:40 no report of what he said had appeared in the sources checked, so his words cannot yet be linked to the price. GBP/USD stood near 1.3159 at 19:00, touched about 1.3166 at 19:13 and eased to about 1.3154 by 19:37, a small range that leaves dirhams per pound much as they were. Earlier, BBH said markets had cut the chance of a December Bank of England rise to as low as 70% from 80% after this morning's inflation figures, and it sees support for GBP/USD near 1.3140.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again ahead of the Fed minutes
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3170 at 14:30 Dubai to a low near 1.3152 at about 15:55, recovered briefly to about 1.3162 and stood near 1.3153 at 16:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0970 to 1.0957, so the dip came mainly from a firmer dollar and means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. Investing.com reported the dollar index up 0.3% near 103.7 at 14:35 Dubai, with ING saying markets still price about 75 basis points of further Fed rises and that Governor Waller's call for more rises has focused minds on a longer Fed tightening cycle. No report read names a single item of news behind this afternoon's slide, which came gradually ahead of Governor Bailey at 19:00 Dubai and the Fed minutes at 23:00.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped towards its low for the year, then recovered
feed.text: The pound kept slipping after this morning's softer UK services inflation, and GBP/USD fell from about 1.3170 at 12:00 Dubai to a low near 1.3145 at about 13:05, close to the year's low of 1.3137 named by FXStreet; EUR/USD fell by a smaller share, so this leg was mainly the pound, as markets trimmed the chance of a December Bank of England rise to about 80% from 90%, according to Reuters. From about 13:20 the pound recovered to near 1.3164 by 13:37 while the euro also rose, a modest easing of the dollar as the US ten year yield slipped about one basis point to 5.09%, according to CNBC. No source names a single item of news behind either leg.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped after softer UK services inflation
feed.text: UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%, matching the Reuters poll forecast but below the Bank of England's own 3.7%, while services inflation held at 3.7% against 3.8% expected and core inflation stayed at 2.8% as forecast (ONS, Reuters). Services prices are the part the Bank of England watches most, so a softer reading trims the case for further rate rises and weighs on the pound, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3188 just before 11:00 Dubai to a low near 1.3168 within ten minutes, then settled near 1.3170 to 1.3175, with little further change around Governor Bailey's 11:30 appearance; markets still put about a 90% chance on a Bank of England rise in December, according to Reuters.

feed.title: The dollar has edged higher through the Gulf morning
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from about 1.3196 at 07:38 Dubai to a low near 1.3185 at about 10:30, while EUR/USD fell by a slightly larger share, from about 1.0991 to 1.0977, so the dip came from a firmer dollar rather than the pound and means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. Investing.com reported the dollar index up 0.2% at 103.66 at 08:42 Dubai, near its highest since April 2025, as traders price a Fed rise in December after US import prices rose 1.1% in October against 0.7% expected and New York Fed President Williams said rates would likely need to rise again. No single news item marks the slide, which came gradually ahead of UK inflation figures at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed overnight ahead of UK inflation
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3213 at 20:39 Dubai on Tuesday to a low near 1.3192 at about 04:45 Dubai and stood near 1.3196 at 07:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.1012 to 1.0990, so the dip came from a firmer dollar rather than the pound and means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. Reuters reported the dollar index up 0.1% at 103.66 in early Asian trade, near its highest since April 2025, with the US ten year yield up 2.2 basis points at 5.123% after St. Louis Fed President Musalem said several rate rises may be needed, even as Nvidia's results lifted Asian shares. FXStreet also pointed to a fully priced Fed rise in December and to tension between the US and Iran as support for the dollar before UK inflation figures at 11:00 Dubai.
